root_cause.text: In the rust_binder range allocator, oneway spam detection was implemented incorrectly because `TreeRange::reserve_new()` checked for spam before inserting the new request into the tree, and `ArrayRange` had no equivalent spam-detection path at all.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `oneway_spam_detected` calculation in `tree.rs` from before `self.free_tree.insert(free_tree_node)` to after insertion, and adds a new `low_oneway_space(pid)` check in `array.rs` plus propagates the result through `mod.rs` instead of hardcoding `oneway_spam_detected: false`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the rust_binder range allocator, oneway spam detection was implemented incorrectly because `TreeRange::reserve_new()` checked for spam before inserting the new request into the tree, and `ArrayRange` had no equivalent spam-detection path at all.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves the `oneway_spam_detected` calculation in `tree.rs` from before `self.free_tree.insert(free_tree_node)` to after insertion, and adds a new `low_oneway_space(pid)` check in `array.rs` plus propagates the result through `mod.rs` instead of hardcoding `oneway_spam_detected: false`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update `reserve_new` to return both the reservation result and an additional status flag needed by callers.
intent_record.what: The return type of `reserve_new` was changed from `Result<usize>` to `Result<(usize, bool)>`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now returns an additional boolean alongside the reserved size, allowing callers to distinguish an extra state or outcome from the reservation operation instead of only receiving a single numeric value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add low-space one-way spam detection during buffer reservation by returning a spam flag and checking per-PID allocation thresholds.
intent_record.what: The function `reserve_new` no longer returns միայն `insert_at_offset`; it now computes a `oneway_spam_detected` boolean and returns a tuple `(insert_at_offset, oneway_spam_detected)`. It adds a new helper method `low_oneway_space(&self, calling_pid: Pid) -> bool` that scans `self.ranges`, counts one-way buffers owned by the given PID, sums their sizes, and returns true if that PID has more than 50 buffers or uses more than `self.size / 4` total space. The new logic in `reserve_new` triggers this helper only when `is_oneway` is true and `new_oneway_space < self.size / 10`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, reservation now reports whether the caller is suspected of one-way transaction spamming when async space is low. This enables the caller or higher-level logic to detect abusive allocation patterns based on per-PID buffer usage without maintaining a separate PID map, and it avoids extra work by only scanning allocations once the low-space threshold is crossed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate oneway spam detection from array reservation into the returned success status.
intent_record.what: In the `Impl::Array(array)` branch of `reserve_new`, the call to `array.reserve_new(...)` was changed from returning a single `offset` value to returning a tuple `(offset, oneway_spam_detected)`, and the `ReserveNewSuccess` construction now uses the returned `oneway_spam_detected` value instead of hardcoding it to `false`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the array reservation path can now propagate whether oneway spam was detected by the lower-level allocation logic. This means callers receive accurate spam-detection status for array-backed reservations instead of always seeing it as disabled, which fixes incorrect reporting and any downstream behavior that depends on that flag.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the early oneway spam-detection check from `reserve_new()` and continue allocation without that intermediate test.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the calculation of `oneway_spam_detected` from `reserve_new()`, including the associated comment and the call to `self.low_oneway_space(pid)`. The subsequent code now proceeds directly from computing `new_oneway_space` to matching on `self.find_best_match(size)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer performs the early spam-detection check for oneway allocations when async space drops below the previous threshold. This means `low_oneway_space(pid)` is no longer consulted at this point, so any behavior that depended on `oneway_spam_detected` being set here is disabled or deferred elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add threshold-based one-way spam detection during reservation when async space becomes low.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean `oneway_spam_detected` is introduced in `reserve_new`, computed as `is_oneway && new_oneway_space < self.size / 10 && self.low_oneway_space(pid)`, with an added comment explaining that spam detection starts when async space drops below 20% of remaining async space, and the result is returned in the existing `Ok((found_off, oneway_spam_detected))` tuple.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now only invokes `low_oneway_space(pid)` for one-way allocations when the remaining one-way space falls below a threshold, and uses that result to report whether spamming behavior was detected. This adds conditional spam detection without changing the rest of the reservation flow.

grouping_result.intent: Add threshold-based one-way spam detection during reservation when async space becomes low.
Add low-space one-way spam detection during buffer reservation by returning a spam flag and checking per-PID allocation thresholds.
Remove the early oneway spam-detection check from `reserve_new()` and continue allocation without that intermediate test.
